recipes.name: Dark Chocolate Bacon Cupcakes
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon unsweetened cocoa powder, for dusting

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Place 24 paper liners in two 12-cup muffin tins; coat liners with nonstick spray.
Cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain on paper towels; crumble and set aside.

Whisk flour, sugar, ¾ cup cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl. Make a well in the center; pour in coffee, buttermilk, oil, and eggs. Stir just until blended. Mix in ¾ bacon; reserve ¼ for garnish. Divide batter among the prepared cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until tops spring back when lightly pressed, 20 to 25 minutes.

Cool in tins set on a wire rack. When cool, arrange cupcakes on a serving platter; frost with your favorite chocolate frosting. Sprinkle reserved bacon crumbles on top; dust with remaining 1 tablespoon cocoa powder.

raw_recipe.headline: Dark Chocolate Bacon Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: This dark chocolate bacon cupcake recipe features unsweetened cocoa powder, strongly brewed coffee, smoky bacon, and buttermilk for a taste-bud adventure.

video.description: Get ready for a rich chocolate and smoky bacon flavor explosion.

review.reviewBody: WOW! If you LOVE Chocolate and you LOVE Bacon you have to try this! This definitely is the perfect marriage of sweet and salty. My husband thinks bacon should be a food group so I thought I'd surprise him with this for his birthday instead of making a regular 'ol birthday cake. This definitely fit the bill. The cake in and of itself is beyond moist and chocolately. You could tell that right away from the buttermilk and oil that it was going to be good. I used 1 cup of Hershey's cocoa but other than that didn't change a thing. I think I'll use this cake recipe with or without the bacon because it was so rich and decadent! I didn't want huge chunks of bacon in this so I put the bacon in a mini-food processor and then added it to the batter. I didn't want to do small cupcakes because I needed a "WOW" factor so I made a dozen Texas sized cupcakes in a oversized muffin pan. They took a little longer to bake but ended up looking like mini-cakes. I iced them with "Rich Chocolate Frosting" from this site which is to die for and toppped them with the additional crumbled bacon. When I tried one for the first time I thought why not have these for breakfast - it's got everything...coffee and bacon. Definitely a case of "don't knock it 'til ya try it"!

I made these cupcakes for my dad's and best friend's birthday, and they were amazing!! Like others have said, the bacon MUST be crispy or else the cupcake has a whole different taste. And it wouldn't hurt to add in a little extra bacon, either. I also used about a teaspoon more baking soda, and it provided a fluffier texture that tasted great. I would recommend a light, chocolate buttercream frosting for this recipie to further the constrast between the sweetness of the cake and the saltiness of the bacon. Overall, I loved these cupcakes, and ai will definitely be making these again!

These were very good. To add a little more bacon flavour I substituted 1 tsp of bacon fatfrom the cooked bacon for 1 tsp of vegetable oil. Also used 1 tsp of the bacon fat in the butter frosting I made. They turned out perfect. Not to sweet.

I made this for my husbands birthday, and he loved it! I did two things different, I made this into a cake instead of cupcakes, and I used a pound and a half of bacon- because bacon is just awesome. Everything else I kept the same.

This is an amazing recipe! Everyone who had one came back for more, and brought friends!

Now for the tips/tricks: I took the advice of previous reviewers and brewed my coffee very, very strong and made sure the bacon was really, really crispy. Rather than frying it up, I followed the directions on the back of the bacon package to cook on a cookie sheet in the oven, which worked very nicely. Also, to get the pieces as small as possible, I used a food processor to crumble, which also worked nicely. 

I chose to make mini-cupcakes instead of regular sized. If you decide to go this direction, I baked mine for 12 minutes and they came out done, but still moist. However, I would shy away from making this recipe as minis again. The flavor of the cake was spot on, but in the smaller size when frosted, the cake to frosting ratio (even with minimal frosting) skewed the overall flavor and made the bacon hard to detect. After extensive testing by my volunteer tasters, it was agreed that a regular size cupcake would create the best balance.

This recipe was amazing! my cousin was having a pig roast party, and we thought that this would be very fitting with the theme.

I made this cupcake recipe into a cake using 1 1/2 recipes yielding a 3 layer 8 inch cake. I used chocolate peanut butter frosting in between the layers as well as a coat of chocolate ganache between each layer. As an after thought a nice salted caramel could have worked as well.

Do not be afraid to try this recipe, it'll be a crowd pleaser :)

The cupcake recipe itself is 5 stars, delicious. The bacon was an unusual texture to come across while eating a cupcake, not much to our liking. I will definitely make this again, but I'll probably add chocolate chips instead of bacon to the batter. The bacon on top was ok, but I would also add or sub chopped nuts. My youngest spit out the bits of bacon and I have to say in all my years of motherhood that was a first for me!

The chocolate cake itself was good, I may try it without the bacon. None of us cared for the texture or flavor of the bacon with the chocolate - it just didn't work to run across the pieces of bacon in with the cupcakes - I chopped it quite fine and cooked it well, but it was just an odd texture in a cupcake. No thanks!

Coming back to say I tried the recipe again without bacon and the cupcakes were fantastic - the coffee really gives the chocolate flavor some "oomph" and the cupcakes were so moist. I frosted them with "Rick's Special Butercream Frosting" from this site, adding 3 Tbsp. cocoa powder and using 1/2 butter and 1/2 shortning instead of all shortening like it called for. Guests at my party loved them.

I made these for a birthday. My family really liked the cupcakes frosted with chocolate ganache frosting. I would make them again, but if I used bacon, I would only sprinkle it on top. Even though I chopped it finely, as others suggested, we didn't like the texture of the bacon in the cupcake itself.

These are pretty much perfect! I did add about half a teaspoon of vanilla for a little bit more balance but other than that it was great. I also made a homemade maple buttercream instead of just plain chocolate icing and it was a beautiful pairing. This recipe is awesome and not hard at all to make. I would highly recommend it! I'm fairly certain my husband just fell in love with me all over again after eating one

Made these as written. Everyone loved them. Texture is great, smell is wonderful, flavor is top notch. We could taste the chocolate, hint of coffee, bacon on top was a great touch. Chocolate Coffee Buttercream Icing recipe on this site was perfect topping.

I thought these were really good! I did replace the half a cup of oil with 1/4 cup of oil and a 1/4 cup of melted butter. I also didn't need a whole tablespoon of cocoa powder for dusting, probably like a teaspoon and a half was all I used. I could taste the bacon in most of the bites there were some bites that didn't have any bacon flavor but overall it was pretty good.
Love these! Followed another reviewer's advice and chopped the bacon before frying. This made the perfect little crispy bacon bits. Topped these with a chocolate buttercream.
Excellent. No changes or subs.

Moist and good. Next time I make these I am going to use Jalepeno Bacon to give it a little kick. I'll also increase the amount of bacon as it wasn't as baconeee as I'd like. But for all intense purposes - this is a fantastic recipe.

These were interesting. My family had mixed feelings. My husband thought more bacon. My dad thought no bacon. I think they are ok, but not as moist as I would have liked. I think next time I would add an extra egg.
tastes terrible! DO NOT EAT!

Made as directed. Too dense. Only needed 15 minutes to bake. Bacon doesn't really have flavor in batter. To be honest not worth the calories to eat them all. Batter made 2 dozen regular cupcakes and 2 dozen mini cupcakes.
I've made these cupcakes more then once and have been excited to do it again. This weekend I'll be serving these for a graduation party.

I have to admit that I did add a little bacon grease to my frosting to enhance the hickory smoked taste and a little extra salt to the crumbled bacon. I still don't think they would have tasted that great, had I not deviated from the recipe, though. 
 I made them along with another flavored cupcake for dessert at one of my gatherings. I ended up throwing them away after watching their faces wince, as though biting a piece of liver. So disappointing. I love both chocolate and bacon, so I can't understand why these weren't a hit.
